findings.title: async forEach callback breaks the enclosing try/catch, silently swallowing calendar/video cleanup errors
findings.body: The `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(...)` call (line 125) is wrapped in a `try { ... } catch (error) { logger.error(error.message) }` (lines 124-139). The PR makes the forEach callback `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `Array.prototype.forEach` never waits for or propagates the promises returned by its callback, so if `getCalendar` or the subsequent `calendar.deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` call rejects, that rejection now escapes as an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding try/catch. Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous, so a thrown error propagated synchronously through `forEach` straight into this same catch block and was logged. After this change, failures during reschedule cleanup of calendar/video events are silently lost (no log, potential unhandled-rejection crash) rather than being handled as before.

findings.title: async forEach callback breaks the enclosing try/catch, silently swallowing calendar/video cleanup errors
findings.body: Identical issue as in vital/lib/reschedule.ts: the `forEach` callback at line 125 was made `async` to accommodate the now-async `getCalendar`, but `forEach` does not await or propagate the callback's promise, so errors thrown inside (e.g. from `getCalendar` or `calendar.deleteEvent`) now become unhandled promise rejections instead of being caught by the `try/catch` at lines 124-139 that previously caught them when `getCalendar` was synchronous. This is a regression in error visibility for reschedule cleanup of stale calendar/video events.

findings.title: forEach(async ...) fire-and-forgets calendar/video cleanup with no error handling in requestReschedule
findings.body: Line 553 changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => {...})` into `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` to allow the now-async `getCalendar` call on line 556 to be awaited. There is no try/catch around this block. Previously, since `getCalendar` was synchronous, a thrown error would propagate out of `forEach` and reject the enclosing async tRPC mutation, surfacing a failure to the client. Now, any rejection from `getCalendar`/`calendar.deleteEvent` inside the async callback is an unhandled promise rejection that never reaches the mutation's caller: the reschedule request can report success even though the old booking's calendar/video event was never actually cleaned up, and no error is logged anywhere.

findings.title: Object literal with eager `import()` calls does not provide lazy loading, yet forces async access everywhere
findings.body: `appStore` is defined as an object literal whose property values are `import("./app")` expressions. Because object literals are evaluated immediately, every one of the ~28 `import()` calls fires as soon as any file does `import appStore from "@calcom/app-store"` (or `@calcom/core/videoClient`, etc.) — exactly as eager as the previous static imports. This gives none of the deferred/on-demand loading benefits typically associated with dynamic import (e.g. `() => import(...)` invoked only when a specific app is actually needed), yet it forces every call site across the codebase (CalendarManager, EventManager, videoClient, handleCancelBooking, handleNewBooking, bookings.tsx, payment handlers, getCalendar) to become `await`-based, adding overhead and the error-handling regressions noted elsewhere in this review, without delivering the stated goal.

findings.title: No tests added for a cross-cutting async refactor of appStore access
findings.body: This PR changes the type of every `appStore[key]` access from a directly-usable module object to a `Promise`, forcing `await` in a dozen call sites spanning booking cancellation, rescheduling, calendar, video and payment flows. None of the 12 changed files are tests, and no new/updated tests accompany this refactor. The forEach/async regressions identified in vital/wipemycalother reschedule.ts and bookings.tsx (where error handling silently breaks) would likely have been caught by tests exercising calendar/video deletion failure paths during cancellation/reschedule.

findings.title: Possible incomplete migration: other appStore consumers outside this diff may still assume synchronous access
findings.body: The exported shape of `appStore` changed from directly usable namespace objects to `Promise`s that must be awaited before use. Only 12 files are updated in this PR, but `@calcom/app-store` is referenced throughout the monorepo (app installation/configuration flows, OAuth callback routes, admin app pages, event-type app settings, etc.) that are not part of this change set. Any such file that still does `appStore[key].lib...` without `await` will now receive a pending `Promise` instead of the resolved module, which will either fail type-checking (if strongly typed) or silently misbehave at runtime wherever indexing bypasses the type system (e.g. via `any`/loose casts). The PR description and diff don't show that every usage of `appStore` in the repo was audited/updated.

findings.title: getVideoAdapters now resolves app modules sequentially instead of concurrently
findings.body: `getVideoAdapters` was converted from a synchronous `reduce` into a `for...of` loop that does `await appStore[appName...]` once per credential (lines 24-33). Since each `appStore[appName]` is a module-level promise, awaiting them sequentially inside the loop adds one microtask tick per credential instead of resolving all of them concurrently with `Promise.all`. For call sites with many credentials (e.g. `getBusyVideoTimes`), this introduces unnecessary sequential latency compared to a `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))` approach.
